contracts.title: CSM14-09 · 26 Jun 2028 — Close rebase authorization and publication races (180m)
contracts.implementation_task: Strengthen the acceptance boundary with the existing current-authorization generation/public access guard and execute a deterministic revocation-versus-accept schedule. A previously authorized preview must not grant later mutation rights. Use the established same-database serialization/guard mechanism rather than holding a client-side flag. Extend the UI regression to ensure late private refresh responses cannot populate another signed-in owner’s view.
contracts.fixture: A is authorized at authorization generation 4 and receives a preview. The prepared schedule revokes the relevant access at generation 5 before acceptance reaches its commit decision. Another schedule keeps authorization at 4 and succeeds. A late response from A then arrives after an existing session switch to B. Only synthetic owner/source markers are present.
acceptance: When revocation is ordered before the acceptance decision, no new checkpoint/audit domain effect or private response is produced for the revoked actor.
When acceptance serializes before a later revocation, the receipt describes that precise order; the subsequent revoked read is denied. No impossible retroactive rollback guarantee is claimed.
An unchanged-authority control case can still succeed; the fix is not blanket denial.
B never sees A’s branch/operation identifiers or private selection context from a late response; public catalog data remains separately scoped.
The regression records the actual barrier/transaction schedule and server enforcement point; client cancellation alone is insufficient.
contracts.architecture_evidence: Record a happens-before diagram with the current-authorization check and transaction decision. Explain the limited, testable revocation guarantee and the alternative behavior if no serializable authoritative guard is available.
contracts.novelty: This is a new mutation authorization race over branch acceptance, rather than repeating read-only explorer cache/authorization-generation mocks.

contracts.title: CSM14-10 · 27 Jun 2028 — Evolve checkpoint provenance without breaking readers (180m)
contracts.implementation_task: Add one backward-compatible optional provenance code to resolved checkpoint metadata using the supplied migration harness: LOCAL_UNCHANGED, UPSTREAM_REFRESH or EXPLICIT_CONFLICT_CHOICE. Historical rows are UNKNOWN/UNRECORDED, never guessed. Implement the additive PostgreSQL migration and typed API/React compatibility seam without changing immutable source references or requiring a new service. Use prepared copies of the day-7 consumer and current consumer to exercise old/new payloads.
contracts.fixture: Prepared r1 lacks provenance; r2 has an upstream refresh and an explicit conflict choice. One response adds the optional field to schemaMajor 1; one has an unsupported required schema major. The disposable database starts from the pinned pre-migration schema and includes the existing immutable row hashes.
acceptance: Migration preserves existing revision/source identity and data; old rows remain explicitly unrecorded rather than labeled as independently resolved.
The prepared older compatible consumer tolerates the optional field under its actual contract; if it does not, record the incompatibility instead of claiming compatibility.
The new consumer reads old payloads with Unknown provenance and rejects an unsupported required schema major safely.
A migration failure leaves the disposable database in a known rolled-back or explicitly failed state; no destructive rollback of retained history is attempted.
Record the actual old/new application-schema compatibility matrix and commands; this local test is not a deployment or rollback guarantee.
contracts.architecture_evidence: Retain the two-consumer/two-payload compatibility matrix and the expansion decision. Explain what a backward-compatible optional field can preserve and why it cannot manufacture historical evidence.
contracts.novelty: This evolves a real artifact built in this sprint, rather than repeating a detached schema-expansion or lineage exercise.

contracts.title: CSM14-11 · 28 Jun 2028 — Measure bounded refresh-history query behavior (180m)
contracts.implementation_task: Implement or refine the owning Shortlist history/read adapter to return a bounded 20-revision page and fetch at most three current source references through the Catalog public batch port. Eliminate only a demonstrated N+1 or unnecessary scan in this new checkpoint path. Compare one narrow index/query alternative against the baseline using the prepared identical synthetic datasets and supported PostgreSQL plan tools.
contracts.fixture: Prepared datasets contain 100 and 1,000 immutable checkpoint revisions for A, matching rows for B, and three public source families. Page size is 20 with deterministic revision ordering. Each before/after run uses the same dataset, candidate settings, warmup and request accounting; at most five measured executions per condition. This is a local synthetic experiment, not load testing a live service.
acceptance: The page contains only A’s requested checkpoint revisions with stable order and no repeated/missing rows in the fixed fixture.
Public-port call counters prove the declared bounded lookup count; private ownership is not dropped to obtain a faster plan.
Save actual EXPLAIN/query metrics, rows examined/returned and all failure counts for matched runs; label cold/warm conditions and tiny sample limits.
The chosen optimization must retain correctness and show its measured trade-off, including no improvement if that is the result.
No distributed cache, new database, broker or paid infrastructure is introduced to satisfy this bounded workload.
contracts.architecture_evidence: Write a brief measured decision record with workload, query count, actual plan observation, storage/write cost of the candidate index and a falsifying workload. Do not extrapolate 1,000 local rows to production capacity.
contracts.novelty: The measurement is attached to the newly implemented branch-checkpoint history API, not a generic cache cost model or misleading-benchmark review.

contracts.title: CSM14-12 · 29 Jun 2028 — Implement a differential branch-history checker (180m)
contracts.implementation_task: Author a small executable reference state model independently of the production rebase implementation, then replay bounded command schedules through both model and actual application service. Compare immutable history/head, operation outcomes and source identities. Use state-table rules, not production helper methods, as the oracle. Add one regression for any genuine difference; do not manufacture a defect or silently change the oracle to match the candidate.
contracts.fixture: Use two local branches, two catalog generations and at most six commands per trace. The instructor supplies 12 finite seeded schedules combining expected-revision conflict, same-key retry, changed-key payload conflict and rollback; the learner authors four additional fresh schedules before inspecting production results. All reset/seed mechanics are already prepared.
acceptance: The independent reference model predicts each trace before the production run and declares any simplifying assumptions.
Every accepted operation creates at most one durable revision/effect; rejected/conflicting/rolled-back operations preserve the expected old head and required atomic records.
A deliberately defective disposable candidate fails at least one checker assertion for the intended semantic reason; the normal candidate result is recorded honestly.
The checker reports the earliest divergent command and exact state difference without dumping private payloads.
Guidance, shared implementation logic or disclosed fault mechanisms are recorded; they cannot be mislabeled independent model design.
contracts.architecture_evidence: Explain the model’s abstraction boundary, the independent oracle’s weaknesses and what its bounded traces cannot prove. Include one counterexample that would pass a simple final-row-count assertion but fail this history checker.
contracts.novelty: This new differential checker analyzes the complete branch acceptance protocol, rather than redoing a portfolio evidence checker or a general debugging interview.
